answers_to_author_questions.Q1_emergency_clause_Art12: Risk currently exceeds benefit. Prefer a rigid Constitution plus honest BLOCK over an elegant escape valve. If kept, require the three cumulative conditions (signal, ledger, short non-renewable expiry) and treat any use as an incident. I would not block the rest of the critique on this; I would withhold P-12 until a concrete need appears.
answers_to_author_questions.Q2_Lacuna1_Art13: Making Articles 1 and 2 non-derogable is correct. When an order conflicts with a non-derogable article, the system must BLOCK and record, not choose. That is safer than silent exception. No case I see makes the system unusable; it makes the conflict visible to the owner.
answers_to_author_questions.Q3_sanction_unimplemented_mechanisms: Approve them now as TARGET objectives written into the Constitution, but label the implementation gap explicitly in the threat/risk register so a permanent violation is not normalised. A written requirement that guides implementation is better than waiting; a written requirement treated as already true is worse. Prefer the first.
